knowledge_gaps: The proposed mining curriculum advances beyond the starting loss/count experiment without establishing that uniform K=16 CE and its count-matched baseline-objective control have been evaluated. Preserve those comparisons or explicitly limit claims to the combined intervention.

The 20-epoch warm-up, pool size 32 and ranks 9/13/17/21 lack supporting evidence. Pool-relative ranks do not guarantee meaningful hardness, especially with duplicate candidates or tied scores. Early stopping before epoch 21 would prevent testing the intervention.

Reproducing model-dependent mining requires recording the pool, actual detached mining scores, selected indices, tie handling and final candidate multiset. RNG information and final logits alone cannot reconstruct selection from an earlier model state.

The core helper assumes predict_score supports row-specific candidate matrices; the supplied compatibility contract does not establish that shape behavior. Diagnostic transport, baseline reduction, fallback behavior and fresh-process predictor verification remain integration specifications rather than implemented steps.

Equal final candidate counts do not imply equal computation. Report mining overhead and GPU-seconds alongside fixed-step validation comparisons. The report also omits paired validation uncertainty and an explicit remaining-budget allocation.

Originality 3 is defensible for an established sampling adaptation. Potential 7 remains speculative, while difficulty 4 may understate production-record capture and audit integration. False negatives, popularity shortcuts and adaptive validation overfitting remain unresolved; missing diagnostic coverage provides no evidence favoring harder negatives.
